messages:
Maya: heads up - seeing a 30-40ms tail regression on hosted text-generation after yesterday's ingress change. p95 stable, p99 up.
Jon: can you paste the flamegraph/heatmap?
Maya: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/397531 - flame shows host parse hot on 'req_unmarshal' and a big stack on tokenization.hold_and_copy
Maya: config: dedicated small requests (avg tokens 18), burst 100r/s. repro route: /v1/generate (streaming)
Sasha: do you see more syscalls? last time writev fallback caused tiny writes and killed tail latencies :confused: 
perf-bot: bench/ingress-latency v2 results available in perf dashboard
perf-bot: p50 12.3ms | p95 22.1ms | p99 78.9ms (baseline p99 ~45ms)
Lee: quick strace snippet shows repeated recvmsg + memcpy + free for each chunk, lots of small allocations
Lee: kprobe summary: 3.2M small allocs in 10s window on ingress worker (size < 512B)
Jon: likely host-side tokenization + proto unpacking combined with KV cache miss churn. small seqs pick fast kernels, so kernel time small and host overhead dominates
Maya: repro command (local):
```
# minimal repro - streaming batch of small prompts
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  echo -n '{"prompt":"hi"}' | grpcurl -plaintext -d @ localhost:8080 inference.Inference.Generate
done
```
Jon: try lazy-unmarshal patch I prototyped: avoid copying proto bytes into strings until tokenization touches them
Jon: also try bumping batching heuristic to prefer batch size 8 for these short sequences (helps amortize host overhead)
Sasha: there's an interaction with kernel selection: small sequences select the 'fast-gemm' codepath which completes quickly but amplification of host overhead becomes visible
Lee: I ran an A/B locally: lazy-unmarshal reduced p99 by ~26% (baseline p99 78ms -> 58ms) but p50 unchanged
Maya: confirmed on a canary node: p99 58ms -> 43ms after lazy-unmarshal + header copy dedupe. CPU usage rose ~6% steady-state on ingress worker
Jon: suspected KV cache thrash too: TTLs currently 60s -> many tiny keys evicted. Pre-warm/prefetch on first token might cut misses
Sasha: also seeing extra copies from gRPC metadata duplication. I'll prototype an HTTP2 coalescer that bundles small frames at ingress and dedupes metadata headers
Maya: attached short perf top sample: 
```
   32.4%  req_unmarshal
   18.7%  tokenize_span
   12.0%  kv_cache_miss_path
    7.8%  grpc_metadata_copy
```

Jon: proposed action items:
1) land lazy-unmarshal (low risk)
2) implement ingress frame coalescing (Sasha)
3) adjust batching heuristic to prefer micro-batches of 6-8 for short seq workloads
4) KV cache: add first-token prefetch and reduce eviction churn for small keys

Sasha: will prototype coalescer as a pluggable ingress filter, try dedupe header copies + single writev per request
Lee: I'll experiment with a slab allocator for small request buffers to cut alloc/free noise
Maya: assigning follow-ups: @Sasha lead coalescer + metadata dedupe, @Jon land lazy-unmarshal, @Lee measure allocs and test slab allocator, I'll run a 24h canary sweep once patches land
Jon: quick test locally showed header dedupe + lazy-unmarshal -> p99 43ms, p95 unchanged :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks team. If regression persists after changes I'll open an incident board entry and start rollback plan :eyes:
Sasha: added a short prototype branch: github.com/redwood/inference/tree/ingress-coalesce-proto (WIP)
Lee: note - watch for increased CPU and ensure capacity buckets updated for Dedicated customers
Maya: will monitor. closing the thread unless we see regressions in the canary metrics.
